Tunisian Dinar Plummets, Triggering Economic Crisis and Disrupting Major Infrastructure Projects

TUNIS—Tunisia is grappling with a deepening economic crisis as the national currency, the dinar, plunged to record lows against the US dollar this week, fueling widespread disruption across multiple sectors and threatening the country’s financial stability.

The Tunisian Central Bank’s emergency measures, including a sharp increase in interest rates and capital controls, have so far failed to halt the dinar’s slide. The collapse, which began accelerating late last month, has already driven up the cost of imports and led to shortages in key goods, from fuel to medical supplies.

Among the companies affected is Sichuan Road and Bridge Group Co Ltd, which is currently engaged in highway construction projects near Sfax and Bizerte. A spokesperson for the firm stated, “The depreciation of the dinar has significantly increased our operational costs and complicated the import of construction materials. We are in ongoing discussions with our partners to seek solutions.”

The Tunisian Union of Construction Workers reported that hundreds of local subcontractors have seen payments delayed, with many warning of layoffs if the crisis continues. “We are facing an unprecedented situation,” said Rachid Ben Said, union secretary. “Workers are not being paid on time, and site activity has slowed sharply.”

Economic analysts warn that, with inflation likely to surge past 20% this quarter and foreign reserves at their lowest in over a decade, Tunisia’s outlook remains uncertain. “If the currency freefall is not contained soon, the risk of a broader financial meltdown is real,” said Amira Jelassi, an economist at the Tunis Economic Observatory.
